claims.statement: For fixed network dimension and bounded SIS parameters, the least interval-continuation factor is uniformly finite.
claims.limits: Existence is proved; a useful numerical value is not computed.

claims.statement: A bounded, exactly reconstructible SIS family has continuation factors with exponential lower growth as network dimension increases.
claims.assurance: analytic proof with exact finite cross-checks
claims.limits: The exhibited direction gives the stated rate; no matching upper rate for the optimal factor is claimed.

claims.statement: Symmetric contact matrices in the same admissible box realise the exponential direction in the source residual metric.
claims.assurance: analytic proof and exact rational checks
claims.limits: This is not automatically a lower bound for nonlinear trajectory-error amplification.

claims.statement: Uniformly bounded SIS parameters imply an explicit dimension-free Holder continuation estimate for the residual.
claims.limits: The exponent and constants are not claimed optimal or practically sharp.

claims.statement: The Holder estimate extends to differences of full community-resolved trajectories and to deterministic finite samples with explicit fill-distance and bounded-error terms.
claims.assurance: analytic proof independently re-derived in review
claims.limits: This is not a stochastic observation model and does not apply to aggregate prevalence alone.

claims.statement: The symmetric contact-matrix ambiguity space for a trajectory of span dimension r has dimension (n-r)(n-r+1)/2.
claims.limits: Positive population weights are required for the reconstruction statement.

claims.statement: Nonstationary SIS trajectories can fail reconstruction without a nontrivial block-regular partition.
claims.assurance: analytic proof and exact rational examples
claims.limits: One reduction is an explicit consequence of a 2021 complete-network theorem and is credited accordingly.

claims.statement: All positive nonconstant invariant rays are classified by the displayed algebraic identities, yielding maximal ambiguity families.
claims.assurance: analytic proof with exact finite cross-checks
claims.limits: Historical priority is bounded by the recorded search, not certified exhaustively.
